citation: Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, Government Medical College Srinagar. Antibiogram for the period January 2023 to June 2023 (pus, blood and urine). Srinagar: Government Medical College; 2023.
reporting: Percent susceptible, all locations together. Pus: one list of percentages per organism (organism counts on page 2, no n in the lists). Blood: Gram-positive (MRSA, MSSA, MR-CoNS, MS-CoNS, Enterococcus) and Gram-negative tables without isolate numbers (organism counts on page 6). Urine: Gram-negative table with the number of isolates; Gram-positive table with each organism's share of isolates only.
method: Not stated. The report notes that vancomycin MIC testing (recommended by CLSI for staphylococci) is not done in the laboratory.

verification.note: Scanned PDF, read from page images (scanned PDF). Two separate readings of every table: pass 1 from whole pages rendered at scale 2.5, pass 2 from crops at scale 3 to 4 (wide tables in halves, column headers from rotated crops, a contrast-enhanced crop for the blurred row labels of page 7). The two readings were compared by script: 365 of 365 values and counts agreed. In the blood Gram-negative table (page 8) the unruled Burkholderia row, which has blank cells, was assigned to columns by measuring each value's position against the column positions of the complete E. coli row (grid overlay and ink-segment positions on the deskewed rows). No cell was unreadable except the Enterococcus share of isolates on page 7 (not needed).

notes: Half-yearly antibiogram (January to June 2023) of the Postgraduate Department of Microbiology, GMC Srinagar (cover letter dated 4 October 2023), with sections for pus, blood and urine; no location split, so every row is all settings. The pus lists and the blood tables print no isolate numbers, so those rows have no n; the organism counts of pages 2 (pus) and 6 (blood) are recorded as counts. The urine Gram-positive table prints only shares (Enterococcus 78.4% and S. aureus 21.5% of 293 Gram-positive growths; MRSA 49.2%, MSSA 50.7% of S. aureus), so its rows have no n. Blood shares printed: MRSA 55.17% and MSSA 44.8% of S. aureus (174), MR-CoNS 52% and MS-CoNS 48% of CoNS (201). The pus lists and blood Gram-negative table include "Ceftazidime-tazobactam" / "Ceftazidime+ Tazobactum", which has no drug key and is not recorded. The E. coli and Klebsiella pus lists of the July to December 2023 report repeat several of these figures exactly.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 202 cells (including the seeded 40% sample of 81), all 27 row n values and all 20 counts were read blind from the page images (scale 3 to 5; the unruled tables of pages 7, 8, 10 and 11 at scale 4.5 to 5, with column lines overlaid on pages 7, 8 and 10) and compared with the file by script: 0 differences, nothing corrected.

Stratum checks: the report has no location split, so set "all" is right for every row; specimens (pus samples, blood, urine) and organisms confirmed. Only the urine Gram-negative table prints isolate numbers (278, 69, 65, 8, 5, 6, 1); the other rows have none (n null is right). The blood Gram-negative Burkholderia row (blank cells, no rules) sits under ciprofloxacin 18.1, tigecycline 18.1, levofloxacin 45.4 and cefoperazone-sulbactam 54.5 (printed without a % sign), as recorded.
Cells not kept, re-read: blood Enterococcus amikacin 7.14 (intrinsic, page 7) and urine Acinetobacter (n=8) ciprofloxacin 52 (caution, page 10) are printed that way (source, not transcription).
